rubric.reason: New test `answers 200 when every calendar fails, not an outage-shaped status` (test/google-calendar-routes.test.ts:434-467) asserts only the public HTTP contract: res.status, body.events, body.failedCalendars. No private symbol, no call-count assertion on listEvents, no test name referencing anything the route's public contract does not surface. Consistent with the whole file, read in full.

The new test asserts three independent, falsifiable properties for the all-fail boundary — res.status===200, body.events equals [], body.failedCalendars sorted-equals both ids — matching AC-A8's full observable set; not a tautology, not existence-only, not a same-input restatement of the 1-of-2 case in the same block.

Mocking stays confined to the injected `fetch` global (the established outbound boundary since phase 2), never the SUT (the Hono route). `fetch` is a global function, not a concrete class competing with an interface. The stub is flat URL-routing, no chained `.return_value`. Every test in the block asserts response status/body/outbound-request content, never a bare was-called check.

Plan AC-A8 / PRD AC-11 (API half) remains fully covered and is more precisely covered than before the correction: the block now holds one genuinely-partial-failure test (1-of-2, untouched) plus one genuinely-total-failure boundary test (0-of-2 healthy, new) — replacing a test whose stub, verified directly against src/worker/routes/google.ts:263-265, failed at accessTokenFor and returned before the per-calendar loop ever ran, so it was never actually exercising this block's mechanism. No other AC's coverage was touched: read the full file (25 it() blocks) and confirmed every other describe block matches what the prior APPROVED rounds reviewed; `npm test` independently reports 34/34 files, 598/598 tests passing project-wide, matching the pre-correction baseline with no regression.

Repo-wide grep for `failedCalendars`, every-calendar/all-fail phrasing, and `invalid_grant` turns up no other test — not test/google-calendar-client.test.ts's client-level `distinguishes invalid_grant from a transient failure` (asserts refreshAccessToken's return value, a different SUT/layer entirely), not test/google-settings.test.ts, not test/google-failure-copy.test.ts — covering the route-level all-calendars-fail scenario the new test targets. Separately confirmed the REMOVED test's own duplicate status directly against source rather than taking the manifest's word for it: its stub (`/token` -> invalid_grant/400, else 500) matches the survivor's stub at lines 275-277 exactly, same connect() precondition, same EVENTS route; reading accessTokenFor (src/worker/routes/google.ts:166-180) shows `reason` always flows from `refreshed.reason` independent of the computed status, so the historical status:502/reason:invalid_grant regression the removed test's own source comment cites would satisfy the removed test's not.toBe(200)-plus-regex but fail the survivor's toBe(409) — the removed test could not catch what it claimed to guard, and the survivor already does. Removing it eliminated a real duplicate; the replacement introduces none.
